questions.prompt: What is a solution to a system of equations, on Snellman’s definition?
choices: A Any assignment that satisfies at least one equation.
B An assignment of the variables that satisfies every equation in the system simultaneously.
C The slope of the first equation only.
D A matrix with no entries.
questions.explain: A solution must satisfy all equations at once.

questions.prompt: For two lines in the plane, which solution types does Snellman say are possible?
choices: A Exactly two distinct intersection points always.
B Unique intersection, infinitely many (same line), or none (parallel distinct lines).
C Only infinitely many, never unique.
D Exactly three solutions when slopes differ.
questions.explain: Two lines: one intersection, coincide everywhere, or parallel with no intersection.

questions.prompt: How do linear systems differ from quadratics in the number of solutions, per Snellman?
choices: A Linear systems can have exactly two solutions like many quadratics.
B Linear systems only allow unique, none, or infinitely many—not “exactly two.”
C Quadratics never have solutions; linear systems always have five.
D Both always have exactly one solution.
questions.explain: He contrasts quadratics (which can have two roots) with linear systems’ trichotomy.

questions.prompt: What two solution methods does he demonstrate, and which does he call better for larger systems?
choices: A Only graphing by hand; no algebra.
B Substitution first; then elimination (leading into matrices) as the better scalable method.
C Completing the square for every system.
D Taking logarithms of each coefficient.
questions.explain: After substitution he introduces elimination and matrices as the more powerful approach.

questions.prompt: What real-world relevance does Snellman claim for systems of linear equations?
choices: A They are only historical curiosities.
B Modern GPS (and later fitting/regression ideas) rely on this kind of mathematics.
C They replace all exponential models.
D They forbid using more equations than variables.
questions.explain: He explicitly ties the topic to GPS technology on phones as motivation.
